The source array downloads a prebuilt binary from the project's own upstream GitHub releases page (`https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/download/v$pkgver/koboldcpp-linux-x64-nocuda`) and references two local files (`koboldcpp.desktop`, `koboldcpp.png`) that are part of the AUR package itself.

There is no `pkgver()` function, so no dynamic version calculation executes during sourcing. The top-level scope contains only variable assignments with no command substitution, eval, network calls, or other code execution. All three sources have proper sha256 checksums pinned (the binary is verified, not SKIPped).

The `package()` function contains standard install operations, but these are out of scope for the current gate (`--nobuild --noprepare` skips `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()`). Running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will only fetch the sources and parse the PKGBUILD, neither of which involves executing any untrusted code.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard -bin PKGBUILD with pinned checksums; safe to source and fetch.</summary>
